sections.title: Objective type questions (2 parts of 1 mark, or 4 parts of ½ mark).

questions.q: Two major developments took place in Europe towards the later part of the Renaissance. The first was the ____ Reformation and the second was the ____ Reformation (also called the Counter Reformation).
The literal meaning of Renaissance is ____; it started in ____ around the 14th century A.D.
The first great ____ sculptor was ____ who made the statue 'David'.

Fill in the blanks: The representatives of the 13 colonies called the meeting of the First Continental Congress at Philadelphia in ____ and appealed to the King of England not to impose ____ without their consent.
The ____ Revolution tore down the medieval structures of Europe and brought in new ideas of liberalism and nationalism. France became a republic under ____ Bonaparte.

True or False: (a) The American War of Independence and the French Revolution popularised the feeling of nationalism all over the world. (b) The French revolutionaries were inspired by the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers such as Voltaire, Montesquieu and Rousseau.

Identify the person: (a) He was fearless, believed in the urgent need to unify Germany, and his policy was known as 'Blood and Iron'. (b) The Bolshevik leader who organised the Soviets and replaced the Provisional Government in October 1917.
Fill in the blanks: The spirit of ____ found expression in art and literature. The greatest achievements of Renaissance artists were in the field of ____.
Complete the sentence: The Bolshevik Party headed by ____ organised the Soviet Revolution in ____.

Answer in one word each: (a) Which act of the British Parliament (1765) taxed all business documents and newspapers in the American colonies? (b) What name is given to the dumping of East India Company tea into the sea in 1773?
questions.answer: (a) The Stamp Act (b) The Boston Tea Party

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why did the Renaissance begin in Italy in the 14th century?
questions.answer: Italy was divided into rich city-states such as Venice, which were great trading and intellectual centres where merchants brought wealth and new ideas. These states had political freedom, and new commercial techniques like book-keeping and bills of exchange made Italy prosperous, giving people leisure for study and art.

or.answer: The Counter (Catholic) Reformation was a reform movement within the Roman Catholic Church to reduce corruption and strengthen the Church. It began in Spain, where Ignatius Loyola founded the Society of Jesus, which stressed service of God, charity, chastity and missionary work.

questions.q: Why was the Glorious Revolution of 1688 called 'glorious'? Why did King James II lose the support of his countrymen?
questions.answer: It was called glorious because no blood was shed. James II lost support because of his harsh attitude, the expensive standing army he created and his increasing employment of Roman Catholics in government, army and universities. Parliament replaced him with Mary II and William III.

questions.q: Write two events which marked the beginning of the Modern Age.
questions.answer: (1) The Renaissance, which began in Italy in the 14th century and brought reason, humanism and the spirit of inquiry. (2) The Reformation started by Martin Luther in 1517 and the voyages of discovery, such as Vasco da Gama reaching India in 1498.

questions.q: Why did Europeans discover new lands during the Renaissance?
questions.answer: They wanted a direct sea route to the East for spices, silk, cotton and gems instead of the uncertain route through Arab lands (gold). They also wanted to spread Christianity (God) and win fame (glory). The compass, astrolabe and map-making made the voyages possible.

questions.q: Why was the Renaissance period called the Age of Reason?
questions.answer: Renaissance thinkers rejected blind faith and the authority of tradition. They said knowledge comes from reasoning, observation and experiment, which led to scientific inquiry and discoveries by Copernicus, Galileo and others.

questions.q: Describe the contribution of Michael Servetus and William Harvey to medical science during the Renaissance.
questions.answer: Michael Servetus, a Spanish doctor, discovered the circulation of blood. William Harvey, an Englishman, explained the function of the heart in purifying blood and circulating it through the veins.

questions.q: Mention any two accomplishments in astronomy during the Renaissance.
questions.answer: (1) Copernicus argued that the earth and planets move around the sun. (2) Galileo, using his telescope, discovered the moons of Jupiter, the rings of Saturn and sunspots, confirming Copernicus. (Kepler showed that planets move in elliptical orbits.)

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is the literal meaning of Renaissance, and why did it begin in Italy in the 14th century AD?
questions.answer: Renaissance means 'rebirth'. It began in Italy because: (1) Italian city-states like Venice were rich trading centres where merchants brought wealth and ideas from distant lands; (2) they enjoyed political freedom and a suitable atmosphere for learning and art; (3) new commercial techniques (book-keeping, bills of exchange, public debt) brought prosperity and leisure, and the ruins of Roman buildings revived interest in classical culture.

questions.q: Describe the condition of Italy on the eve of the Renaissance in the 14th century.
questions.answer: Italy was divided into small city-states, many built on the ruins of Roman buildings. Cities like Venice were great centres of trade and intellectual crossroads. The new political and social organisation gave freedom and a good atmosphere for academic and artistic advancement. Trade brought wealth, and people had more leisure for study.

questions.q: Explain the process of the unification of Germany.
questions.answer: Germany was a confederation of 39 states. Kaiser William I of Prussia appointed Bismarck, who modernised the army through his 'Blood and Iron' policy. In 1864 Prussia and Austria defeated Denmark over Schleswig-Holstein; then Prussia defeated Austria and formed the North German Confederation, keeping Italy and France neutral. Finally Prussia defeated France in the Franco-Prussian War of 1871, took Alsace-Lorraine, and the remaining states joined a united Germany under Kaiser William I.

questions.q: Explain the consequences of the Franco-Prussian War of 1871.
questions.answer: (1) France was defeated and Napoleon III abdicated. (2) France had to give up Alsace and Lorraine to Germany. (3) The southern German states joined Prussia and the unification of Germany was completed under Kaiser William I. (4) The unification of Italy was also completed, and Germany emerged as the leading power in Europe.

questions.q: Analyse the contribution of Bismarck to the unification of Germany.
questions.answer: Bismarck, Prime Minister of Prussia, believed unity could come only by 'Blood and Iron'. He strengthened the army even against Parliament. He used diplomacy to isolate enemies — keeping Italy, France and Russia neutral — and fought three wars: against Denmark (1864), Austria (1866) and France (1871). After victory over France, Germany was united under Kaiser William I; hence he is called the 'Iron Chancellor'.

questions.q: What were the main causes of the American War of Independence?
questions.answer: (1) Britain's mercantilist policy did not allow the 13 colonies to set up industries and forced them to sell sugar, tobacco and cotton only to England at fixed prices. (2) Britain taxed the colonies to pay for its wars — the Stamp Act of 1765 and later the tax on tea, which led to the Boston Tea Party (1773). (3) The King treated the Continental Congress's appeal against 'taxation without consent' as rebellion and declared war, leading to the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any six major causes of the Russian Revolution.
questions.answer: (1) Tsar Nicholas II was an autocratic and oppressive ruler who denied people political rights. (2) Workers suffered exploitation, inhuman working conditions and heavy taxes. (3) Peasants did not get proper returns for their produce and famines worsened their condition. (4) Russia entered World War I unprepared; thousands of ill-equipped soldiers died. (5) The government printed millions of roubles, causing inflation and food shortages in cities. (6) The writings of Marx and Tolstoy awakened the workers, who formed Soviets; in February 1917 the Tsar was deposed and in October 1917 the Bolsheviks under Lenin took power.

or.q: Explain the socialist movement and its impact on Russia in six points.
or.answer: (1) The Industrial Revolution created an unequal society of exploited workers and privileged capitalists. (2) Socialism aimed at an equal society. (3) Karl Marx and Engels said history is a history of class struggle (Das Capital). (4) Marx predicted capitalism would end and the state would own the means of production. (5) These ideas inspired Russian workers to form Soviets and demand power. (6) The October Revolution of 1917 under Lenin set up the world's first socialist government and the USSR.

questions.q: How did the French Revolution influence the world? Explain its causes and impact.
questions.answer: Causes: (1) French society was divided into three estates; the clergy and nobility enjoyed privileges while the Third Estate (peasants, workers, middle class) bore heavy taxes. (2) Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette's luxury emptied the treasury. (3) In 1789 the Third Estate declared itself the National Assembly. (4) Thinkers like Voltaire, Montesquieu and Rousseau inspired people. Impact: (5) The Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen asserted equality, sovereignty of the people and rights to liberty, property and free speech; France became a republic. (6) Its ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity, liberalism and nationalism spread across the world and inspired the unification of Italy.

questions.q: What was the Reformation? Explain its causes and impact on Europe.
questions.answer: The Reformation was a religious and political movement that questioned the abuses of the Church. Causes: (1) the Church was associated with superstition, corruption and greed — it sold positions and letters of indulgence; (2) the Renaissance spirit of reason questioned blind faith; (3) in 1517 Martin Luther declared that the Bible was the only authority and salvation came through faith. Impact: (4) Christianity split into Protestants and Roman Catholics; (5) in England the Act of Supremacy made the King head of the Church; (6) the Catholic Church reformed itself through the Counter Reformation and the Society of Jesus.
